items.title: Dit enorme bedrag gaat het nieuwe stadion Club Brugge per seizoen opleveren
items.summary: Het nieuwe stadion van Club Brugge moet niet alleen voor een betere voetbalbeleving zorgen, maar vooral een enorme financiële hefboom worden. Voorzitter Bart Verhaeghe verwacht dat de nieuwe voetbaltempel jaarlijks tot 40 miljoen euro aan extra inkomsten kan opleveren, zegt hij in De Tijd. Dat is volgens hem ongeveer evenveel als wat Club momenteel uit één seizoen Champions League haalt.

items.title: ‘Girl’s day’ controversy reignites debate over how women are treated in South Korean football
items.summary: A referee is alleged to have made a remark referring to menstruation that has revived concerns about treatment of players It was a comment allegedly made by a referee during a WK League match that became one of the biggest controversies in South Korean women’s football. What began as an on-field dispute involving South Korea’s all-time top goalscorer, Ji So-yun, has since developed into a wider debate, prompting a response from the Korea Football Association (KFA) and raising questions about the treatment of female players, the structural set-up of women’s football in Korea and accountability within its governing bodies. It was around the 31st minute of the Suwon FC Women v Seoul City Hall game on 28 August when the incident happened. Suwon’s former Chelsea midfielder Ji appealed for a foul after what she felt were repeated rough tackles by the opposition. The female referee, Bae Sun-young, is then alleged to have made, over the officials’ radio system, a remark interpreted as referring to menstruation after describing Ji as “sensitive from the start”. Ji says she overheard the comment and footage from the game shows Ji visibly upset as she talks to the referee. Ji was shown a yellow card after confronting the official. In frustration Ji threw a water bottle as she approached the Suwon bench. Bae walked towards Ji, appearing to reach for a red card before deciding against issuing one, showing a yellow instead. items.title: Liverpool agree £60m-a-year shirt sponsorship deal with Turkish Airlines

items.title: Champions League is fertile ground for new managers – but knowhow could be key later on
items.summary: Luis Enrique, Vincent Kompany and Mikel Arteta are among the favourites to lead their sides to victory, but more recent appointments should not be counted out A delve into the history of the Champions League shows that managers can and do win in their first season at a club, but also that experience matters. Which makes it interesting, given that tenures for the 2026‑27 crop range from newly appointed coaches to one with almost 15 years in charge. Some have managed more than 100 matches in the competition, others none. It gets under way on Tuesday with 14 of the 36 clubs led by managers who have been in the role for less than a year. It cannot match the turnover of the Premier League, in which 11 of 20 managers were appointed in 2026, but the tenures of the head coaches involved this season break down neatly. Continue reading...
